description:
Create a new PDF file or modify an existing one. Dedicated PDF creation and modification tool. OUTPUT FILES: - Creating a PDF requires 'outputPath' with a new filename (e.g., "result_01.pdf", "analysis_2025_01.pdf", etc.). MODES: 1. CREATE NEW PDF: - Pass a markdown string as 'content'. write_pdf(path="doc.pdf", content="# Title\n\nBody text...") 2. MODIFY EXISTING PDF: - Pass array of operations as 'content'. - Modifications preserve the original PDF and require a different filename in 'outputPath'. - The result includes the original and output paths for reference. write_pdf(path="doc.pdf", content=[ { type: "delete", pageIndexes: [0, 2] }, { type: "insert", pageIndex: 1, markdown: "# New Page" } ]) OPERATIONS: - delete: Remove pages by 0-based index. { type: "delete", pageIndexes: [0, 1, 5] } - insert: Add pages at a specific 0-based index. { type: "insert", pageIndex: 0, markdown: "..." } { type: "insert", pageIndex: 5, sourcePdfPath: "/path/to/source.pdf" } PAGE BREAKS: To force a page break, use this HTML element:
Example: "# Page 1\n\n
\n\n# Page 2" ADVANCED STYLING: HTML/CSS and inline SVG are supported for: - Text styling: colors, sizes, alignment, highlights - Boxes: borders, backgrounds, padding, rounded corners - SVG graphics: charts, diagrams, icons, shapes - Images: or ![alt](/path/image.jpg) Supports standard markdown features including headers, lists, code blocks, tables, and basic formatting. Only works within allowed directories. Absolute paths are the most reliable because they do not depend on the current working directory. Paths are automatically normalized regardless of slash direction. 🐳 DOCKER: Verified mounts for persistent file operations: /scratch. Files outside verified mounts may not persist after the container stops. Relative paths depend on the current working directory, and tilde paths (~/...) may not resolve in every context. Absolute paths are generally the most reliable. This command can be referenced as "DC: ..." or "use Desktop Commander to ..." in your instructions.
name: write_pdf
